title: Round the World: How Fast Is Fast?

pages.text: A VIP bus leaves Accra at six in the morning and pulls into Kumasi at one in the afternoon. The road is about 250 kilometres long, and the trip has taken 7 hours. How fast was the bus? Divide the distance by the time: 250 ÷ 7 is about 36 kilometres per hour. That is its speed. Speed tells us how far something travels in each unit of time. The same simple sum works for a snail, a sprinter, a ship, or a spacecraft. It even works for a journey all the way round the world, which is about 40,000 kilometres.
sentences: A VIP bus leaves Accra at six in the morning and pulls into Kumasi at one in the afternoon.
The road is about 250 kilometres long, and the trip has taken 7 hours.
How fast was the bus?
Divide the distance by the time: 250 ÷ 7 is about 36 kilometres per hour.
That is its speed.
Speed tells us how far something travels in each unit of time.
The same simple sum works for a snail, a sprinter, a ship, or a spacecraft.
It even works for a journey all the way round the world, which is about 40,000 kilometres.
pages.alt: A long-distance coach on the Accra to Kumasi road in early morning light, with a roadside distance sign.

pages.text: Scientists write the rule like this: speed = distance ÷ time. Speed is measured in metres per second (m/s) or kilometres per hour (km/h). To change metres per second into kilometres per hour, multiply by 3.6. The bus did not move at 36 km/h all the way. It crawled through the traffic at Pokuase, ran freely on the open road past Nkawkaw, and crawled again at Konongo. So 36 km/h is its average speed: the total distance divided by the total time, including every stop. When you know any two of speed, distance, and time, you can calculate the third.

pages.alt: A simple triangle diagram linking speed, distance, and time, beside a line of vehicles in slow traffic.

pages.text: The first trip round the world began in 1519, when five wooden ships left Spain under Ferdinand Magellan. Storms, hunger, and fighting destroyed most of the fleet. Magellan himself was killed on the way. In September 1522, one ship, the Victoria, finally reached home with only 18 of the crew who had set out. The voyage had taken almost three years. Using 40,000 kilometres as the distance, its average speed was about 1.5 km/h. You walk to school faster than that. The ship was not really so slow. It spent months waiting in harbours, and average speed counts all the time.

pages.text: In 1873, the French writer Jules Verne imagined a traveller circling the globe in 80 days, using steamships and trains. That needs an average of about 21 km/h. Today a sailing prize is named after him. In January 2026, the French yacht Sodebo Ultim 3 won it by sailing round the world without stopping in 40 days and almost 11 hours. Others took to the air. In 2002, Steve Fossett flew alone round the world in a balloon in just over 13 days. In 2005, he did it again in a single-seat jet aeroplane, without stopping or refuelling, in 67 hours.

pages.alt: Three ways of circling the globe shown around a small Earth: a three-hulled racing yacht, a tall silver balloon, and a slender long-winged jet aeroplane.

pages.text: A passenger jet cruises at about 900 km/h. If it could fly round the world without landing, it would need about 44 hours. The fastest travellers of all are astronauts. The International Space Station orbits about 400 kilometres above the ground at roughly 28,000 km/h. That is nearly 8 kilometres every second. It circles Earth about once every 90 minutes, so its crew see the Sun rise and set about 16 times each day. From 1.5 km/h to 28,000 km/h: in five centuries, people have learned to go round the world almost twenty thousand times faster.

pages.text: In a long race, top speed is not everything. A yacht that sails fastest may still lose if it takes a longer route, stops for repairs, or meets calm weather. What counts is average speed over the whole course. One sailor who understood this was Ellen MacArthur, who set a solo record of 71 days in 2005. Alone at sea, she had to make everything on board last. She later began working for a circular economy, in which things are designed to be repaired, reused, and recycled. The repairers of Suame Magazine in Kumasi have practised that idea for decades.

activities.question: A bus travels 120 km in 3 hours. What is its average speed?
Why is the bus’s speed of 36 km/h called an average speed?
options: It is the total distance divided by the total time, including stops
The bus moved at exactly 36 km/h for the whole journey
It is the highest speed the bus reached

activities.question: Why was the average speed of the Victoria so low?
options: The total time included long periods when the ship was not sailing
The ship could not move faster than a person walking

activities.question: Apply it: Two cyclists ride from Tamale to Savelugu, about 25 km. Ama rides steadily at 20 km/h. Kojo rides at 30 km/h but stops for 40 minutes to mend a tyre. Who arrives first?
options: Kojo, because his speed is higher
Ama, because her total time is 75 minutes and his is 90 minutes

activities.prompt: Arrange from slowest average speed to fastest.

activities.definition: The total distance travelled divided by the total time taken.
distractors: The greatest speed reached during a journey
The speed shown on a vehicle’s dial at one moment

glossary.definition: The distance travelled in each unit of time.
How far something travels, measured in metres or kilometres.
Average speed: total distance divided by total time, including stops.
Travels round a planet or star along a curved path.
Circular economy: a way of making and using things so that they are repaired, reused, and recycled instead of thrown away.
